messages:
Anya: Quick sync — big potential customer (FinX) asked for a low-latency reserved pool + per-route SLAs. They want it gated as an add-on to Enterprise. Thoughts?
Ben: Sounds like Redwood Dedicated features but with tighter latency SLOs and per-route guarantees. What are they willing to pay?
Caroline: They sign for $300k/year committed. Willing to add a recurring add-on for the SLA. Needs clear limits on concurrency and priority routing.
Dan: Finance: we need to model uplift. If add-on = 20% price delta, margin still looks fine given reserved infra. Need assumptions on utilization.
Anya: Proposal draft: add "Priority Pool" add-on (monthly), includes: reserved qps, 99ms p95 for select routes, preemptive capacity during incidents. Limit: 3 routes by default, optional expansion.
Frank: CS: we must add onboarding ops and runbook. FinX will expect a contact and playbook for failover. Also prefer deterministic billing line item.
Eli: Legal: contract constraint — can't promise p95 globally without region/capacity caveats. Need fallback clause and credits formula. Also require data residency clause for EU customers.
Ben: Technical feasibility — runtime can tag routes and route to higher priority pool. Need autoscale guardrails to avoid noisy neighbor. KV cache alignment might cause p95 variance.
Anya: Minimal launch criteria: (1) config UI in Console to create pool + assign routes, (2) infra autoscale + priority routing tests, (3) SLA-credit mechanics documented, (4) CS runbook + 1 pilot customer onboarded.
Caroline: Pilot ask: FinX wants GA in 10 weeks. Willing to go pilot for 6 weeks now. Can we do a pilot-only SKU to mitigate risk?
Ben: 10 weeks is tight but doable if we scope canary: no multi-region support initially, single region EU-west or us-west depending on pilot.
Dan: From billing POV: expose a meter: "priority_pool_hours" + "priority_units_reserved". Pilot should be invoiced as usage + refundable credit if SLA not met.
Eli: Add to contract: pilot clause that limits liability to credits (not > invoice) and time-boxed pilot acceptance tests.
Frank: CS to own pilot success criteria: latency baseline + incident drill. We'll ask FinX for two production routes and traffic sample.
Anya: For limits, suggest default: 3 routes, 500 concurrent tokens/sec pooled, soft cap scaling to 2x with approval. Seats for expansion.
Caroline: Sales note: offer a 6mo pilot discount of 30% on the add-on to accelerate commitment.
Ben: Dev notes: config snippet prototype below — not final but shows routing selector:
```
priority_pool: {
  capacity_units: 500,
  routes: ["/payments/*","/risk/*"],
  p95_target_ms: 99
}
```
Anya: Decision point today: approve pilot scope and contract redlines to start engineering. Vote? (reply with +1 / -1)
Caroline: +1
Ben: +1 (need eng constraints doc)
Dan: +1 if finance model acceptable (I'll sign off by EOD)
Eli: +1 pending legal redline doc (I'll send comments)
Frank: +1 — CS ready to run pilot
Anya: Great — I'll file PRD and schedule kickoff with FinX tomorrow. I'll include the launch checklist and SLA credit formula. :rocket:
Caroline: Adding note: don't forget metric labels for per-route cost breakdown.
Ben: Will add perf tests to eng-releases pipeline and tag the canary.
Anya: Thanks team — closing thread, moving to action items in JIRA.
